title: Lindsey: Drone Orbit
notes: One shot, so cross-shot consistency is not in play -- the only risk is the orbit, which is the move measured to break identity by revealing sides the still never contained. shots.video_prompt: She stays exactly the same size in the frame from the first frame to the last, filling the same amount of the picture throughout, and stays centred in the middle of the frame the whole time. The camera holds at the same height above the grass and the same short distance from her for the entire shot, and slides steadily sideways around her in a smooth arc, so the meadow behind her slides horizontally across the background and her shadow swings slowly around her feet. She turns slowly in place to follow the camera, so her face stays turned up toward the lens for the whole shot. She keeps laughing, and her hair and the hem of her dress move in the wind while the tall grass ripples in long waves around her. Nobody else enters the frame. Everything moves at natural real-time speed, with no slow motion and no speed ramping. Wind across grass, no music.
